svg.text: Kit B: what is in the bag
No breadboard in this kit. Tip everything out and match each thing to a picture. Everything is drawn at the same scale as every later picture.
The computer. Two black strips of sockets (P1, P2) along the long edges,
tiny numbers at the strip ends. Hold it by the edges. The side with the
microSD slot and the dog logo is the side you use.
Must be a data cable. A charge-only
cable looks identical and is the most
Fingernail sized, purple or blue, four pins
(a few have six): VIN or VCC, GND, SCL, SDA
in tiny letters. The small metal can is the
sensor itself. If the pins are loose in the
bag instead of soldered on, stop: that is
A square board with a dark glass window and four pins on
one edge: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA. The order of VCC and GND
differs between makers. Read yours now and write it down.
Getting those two backwards is the one mistake in this
guide that kills a part instantly.
A pin at one end, a socket at the other. Four
needed. The pin end goes into the board's socket;
the socket end slides over the module's pin.
Male-to-male wires will not reach the module.
Female-to-female wires will not reach the board.
No male-to-female wires? A male-to-male wire plus a
female-to-female wire, joined end to end, does the same job.
Not in the bag and not needed: a monitor, keyboard or power supply for the board. Your laptop is all three, through the USB-C cable.
